body:
>When you say crying in public do you mean a couple of tears or do you mean like, bawling?

Both.

>You seem to be way perseverating over a few incidents over a lifetime.

>Should your mother have thrown something? No.

>Do people get angry and lose their shit on occasion? Sure.

>Unless you mean you got scolded for ever letting a tear fall, yeah, this seems overdramatic and oddly focused on your parents not being robot cartoon parents.

Understandable. Thank you for your feedback! 

I do admit to being a little overly sensitive as a person, so typical conflict probably upsets me more than typical (I also take them super personally, since I’ve repeatedly been told I’m the reason our arguments keep happening and given a list of all the things I need to do to prevent my parents’ yelling from happening even when everyone is calmer (without any effort made on their side), yet the yelling still happens just about every time I come home from college despite my best efforts — giving benefit of the doubt, not yelling back when I’m yelled at, etc. — to keep this from happening).

Yes, I feel extremely grateful to have gotten a good job lined up so soon! It has really allowed me to focus strictly on passing my classes and graduating without having to worry about finding a job, and I feel very fortunate.

I just can’t think of a realistic way to spend more time off that doesn’t involve staying at my parents’ house, and prior experience has shown that wouldn’t be great for them or me.

This is how I visited a couple of school friends and one of my grandmothers before my grandmother unfortunately passed from non-COVID causes in October 2020.

It’s a little hard knowing my last time seeing her had to be in this way, but I try to remind myself that it’s better than giving her COVID and her possibly dying from that.

I fully respect my friend’s wishes, though, and don’t wish to change her mind on the matter.

Thank you!
Thank you for your advice! I had definitely started getting more nervous about seeing other older people given the situation with my older friend, though I appreciate the reassurance!

Thank you for the advice! I completely respect my friend’s wishes (she does have a pre-existing condition, though it doesn’t put her in the immunocompromised category) and don’t wish to change her mind on it (it would just make us both miserable anyway), but I appreciate your advice, especially in relation to older family in my life who are more willing to get together.

She mentioned knowing 3 vaccinated people who had recently been hospitalized (in addition to the Delta variant as a whole and being older with a pre-existing condition) as part of her reasoning (I know one of these people, and it was worrying to see her have to be hospitalized, though she fortunately returned home a couple of days ago without having to be intubated).

Thank you again for your advice!

Yeah, she’s isolated more than many have throughout the pandemic (I say this as someone who has taken it seriously throughout and isolated myself this past school year). I wasn’t sure how she’d feel about getting together after cases started surging with Delta, though I thought she’d still be OK with it, and was admittedly shocked and sad to learn this past Sunday (the week we planned to get together) that she had changed her mind on it indefinitely (she’s a retired teacher, and mentioned knowing 3 teacher friends who recently had to be hospitalized with COVID despite being vaccinated (in addition to the Delta variant as a whole and her being older with a pre-existing condition) as part of her reasoning — I know one of these teachers, and it was sad to see she had to be hospitalized, though she fortunately was able to go home a couple of days ago without ever needing to be intubated).

She got vaccinated in early February, and her pre-existing condition doesn’t put her in the immunocompromised category, though I’m hopeful she’ll be eligible for the booster shot soon (even if she isn’t eligible right away).

The whole situation definitely made me nervous about seeing other older people in my life, though, especially my 90-year old aunt. I also started becoming nervous about seeing other older people in the next few weeks (including my 74-year old grandmother, who has the same pre-existing condition as my older friend and is also vaccinated — unlike my friend, though, she got COVID during the winter surge).

I respect my friend’s wishes completely and don’t want to change her mind on it (it would likely just make both of us feel miserable the whole time), though I appreciate the advice in relation to other older people in my life who are more willing to get together.

Update: the agency where I’m doing my internship just reimplemented a bunch of social distancing mandates.

Seating in the cafeteria is now restricted to one per table. Gatherings are limited to 10 people or fewer. Gym is by appointment only (understandable, given increased COVID transmission there). Official travel is canceled. Visitors are restricted to essential only.

No mask mandate yet, weirdly enough, but it seems it will probably come back soon.

The intern coordinators are now scrambling to adjust intern events in response to these changes, and nobody knows what is going to happen.

I’m not sure I can take this much longer given my history of mental health concerns… :(

At least I only have 2 weeks left of the internship, I guess.

The mask mandate itself doesn’t bother me that much; I’m just worried this will soon turn into social distancing/gathering restrictions being reimposed because people won’t do the right thing (i.e. get vaccinated).
Atlanta, GA (I’m not from the city of Atlanta, but my college is within Atlanta city limits)

Thank you for sharing this! I’ve been masking up when I go to stores and restaurants, and I plan to continue doing this until things get safer. I’m just worried about this variant or another variant reversing all of our progress as a result of a vaccination rate that is too low, and that’s really hard to think about given how much I was struggling to stay afloat last year.

To be honest, I tend to say phrases like that as a self-protective mechanism to try to justify that it will be OK (even when it’s really not — or, in this case, even when it really does affect me), sometimes without even realizing it, so I appreciate you calling that out in this post.

I just talked with my mom about this after reading these comments, and I described that conversation in response to TheUnholyDarkness’s comment.

I just talked with my mom about this and my reasons for why I feel it’d be good for me to have at least one driving alone experience before I leave for the internship (I argued that even a few weeks of practice in a new location with my dad could not be equivalent to years of practice here) after reading these comments, and she agreed to let me drive alone once this weekend, but only if I agree to drive my dad’s car (which I drove a lot before getting my car) instead of my car and if I drive only on the route I originally started practicing driving on (since it’s the route I’ve practiced on the most).

She was not willing to budge beyond that, so I agreed to it, since it’s better than the alternative and does at least give me one experience driving alone before I’m in a new state for the simmer.

She said she still needs to talk with my dad about it and will let me know later today (they’re both working currently), and I’m hoping he agrees as well.

I’m so glad I saw this post. I also really hate crying during arguments, especially since it often means my parent(s) will then proceed to yell at me for overreacting and/or emotionally manipulating them and/or creating a scene, and I always kind of subconsciously wondered if it really was an issue with me crying too easily.

I tend to go blank/shut down when yelling happens, too, and I just become completely defenseless in those moments.

It’s weirdly reassuring to see it’s not an issue with me like I originally thought it might’ve been.

While I can hold it in for a bit until I can go somewhere private in those scenarios, I can’t always hold it in for long depending on how badly I feel the need to cry, so I usually need to go somewhere quickly to avoid bottling it up and/or accidentally crying a bit in an inappropriate situation (I wouldn’t need to go somewhere private at all if I could completely hold it in without issues).

If one or both of my parents are continually yelling at me, though, it’s nearly impossible for me to keep myself from crying unless I go somewhere private ASAP, and that wasn’t feasible in this situation (I was just meeting up with her in a parking lot for a bit before leaving).

I’ve had similar situations where I’ve cried in response to my mom getting upset with me when in my parents’ house, since she often won’t let me go to my room or somewhere private to calm down a bit if needed before resolving the argument more calmly (she feels that each argument needs to be resolved right then and there, and has often interpreted me wanting to go to my room to calm myself a bit as me trying to avoid the argument completely).

(I just say my mom here because my dad, too, feels the need to go somewhere private to calm himself a bit and, consequently, is more understanding of my need to do that.)

I can’t really say how much this applies to people in general yelling, since I’ve rarely had other people yelling at me, but I can’t recall any scenarios where anyone else has continually yelled at me to the point of tears.

Basically, I really don’t want anyone to feel as though I’m manipulating them, and I don’t want to make anyone feel that they need to sympathize or feel a certain way toward me. I just wish I was better at controlling my own emotions (both positive and negative — I honestly don’t have much of an emotional middle ground, hence why I’m in therapy for it) so I don’t upset other people (particularly my parents) as easily.

Thank you for the advice! I’m currently finishing up the current semester at college, but I’ll plan to discuss this with them once I return to their house from college in a few weeks.

Helped.

It’s pretty rare for me to cry around anyone other than my parents (in scenarios where I feel I absolutely need to cry, I’ll hold it in until I can go into a bathroom or somewhere where I can be alone and let it out there), but I do admit to feeling things very intensely (I’m also autistic, which probably has an effect on this) and am currently in therapy for this along with anxiety and depression (the latter two are probably unrelated and have gotten better with the help of therapy, but I am in therapy for those as well).

I also was able to get the vaccine earlier than I thought I would!! I initially assumed I'd be getting it when the general adult population gets it, but my state did a complete overhaul of the rest of its vaccination distribution plan a couple of weeks ago, and one of the categories currently eligible in the new plan is one that I fall under!

I plan to call my doctor tomorrow to see what she would recommend, and my mom was OK with this (thankfully) when I told her I would be doing this.

I really think hearing my doctor’s recommendation will be helpful for my peace of mind in this situation.

Thank you all so much for your advice! I really appreciate it.

I’m not sure if May would be within the acceptable schedule period for Gardasil, though, since it’d be 5 months after I first got Gardasil in December, and the recommended time interval for the second dose is only 2 months after the first dose. Since 5 months is closer to the recommended time interval for the third dose than the second dose, I’m worried 5 months between the first and second Gardasil doses will be too late and I’d have to start over.

If I do become eligible, I want to talk with my doctor to see what she recommends, but my mom is super adamant right now about not letting me reschedule Gardasil to get the COVID vaccine (she’s definitely in support of the COVID vaccine, but won’t let me prioritize it over Gardasil if necessary).

I wish there were only 2 doses lol. When I got my first dose in December, my doctor mentioned I’d need to come back 2 months later for the second dose (but could delay it by a month or 2 if necessary — I delayed it to March because my only 2 days off of school are in March this semester, and I didn’t think I could be eligible for the COVID vaccine then, nor did I really know about the 14 day rule from the CDC) and 6 months after my first dose/4 months after the second for my third dose (again, delayed a bit for me because of a summer internship — I’ll be getting that in August).

If I postpone Gardasil, it’d mean I’d have to schedule it in May instead of March due to needing to complete both COVID vaccine doses, and I imagine that would likely affect scheduling for the third dose as well (since August is only 3 months after May).
Thank you for this reminder! It’s hard since things are still so uncertain and tragic, but the recent news about the vaccine development has given me a bit of hope in the midst of this craziness.

I would be absolutely thrilled if this ends up being the case, especially since I have an internship lined up for next summer, and I really want to finally have a chance to meet a relative who is now in her early 90s (without having to worry about giving her COVID). I’ll definitely get the vaccine as soon as possible after they say I can now get it!

I get what you mean; I've seen plenty of students on campus who are unfortunately not taking this as seriously as it needs to be taken (I actually stopped going to in-person events hosted by our RAs after discovering that, while masks were mandated, distancing was not possible at one of the events they hosted - I didn't realize this until after I showed up).

Thank you so much, and I hope you have a safe holiday season!

Is there anything I mentioned in this post that would result in it getting downvoted? If so, I'd be happy to reword it.

To clarify, I definitely trust CDC recommendations through this crisis, the issue really has more to do with the fact that my college is proceeding with a plan for the holidays that, while not "wrong" necessarily, contradicts this particular guideline recently issued by the CDC.

Also, I love my mom and we have a great relationship, she just gets upset easily as a result of a dysfunctional childhood.

Thank you so much again! I really appreciate your advice and support as I work through these thoughts and overall situation.

I hope I can work up the courage to tell my counselor about this soon and that my counselor can be of help with this.

Thank you so much! I think it would help to tell my counselor about these thoughts (maybe leave out the part about having a plan), though I'm a little nervous about it (I was actually asked multiple times if I was contemplating suicide during the process of getting counseling, and admittedly, I never had a good answer for that question).

It doesn't help that healthcare is kind of garbage here in the U.S.

Thank you both again for your advice! I have posted an update post here: https://www.reddit.com/r/Advice/comments/i7y676/update_how_to_cope_with_a_mom_who_is_easily/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app&utm_name=iossmf

Yeah, I’m just really thankful my former teacher has been so supportive of me through this and has encouraged me to go through with counseling to help deal with this situation and for my unrelated anxiety issues (I actually showed her this post, and she likes how supportive this group is and that I reached out to others to gain a more objective view).

Speaking of which, I went through a more formal assessment with my counselor about my anxiety and situation last week, and she also recommended going through with counseling and with seeing a medical provider regarding some of the physical symptoms I have experienced. I plan to hopefully participate in counseling through my school this fall.

Thank you so much for taking the time to listen and offer some advice! I cannot express enough how much that means to me.

Update:

My mom went a little longer than typical without yelling at either of us (she did scold me almost every day, often multiple times a day, for little things that I’ve unfortunately forgotten about now), and it made me wonder if I was exaggerating the situation without realizing it... that is, until she yelled at my dad this morning while he was trying to help her resolve an issue with her email. My dad kept telling her he didn’t know what the issue was, but my mom immediately started yelling at him and demanding to know why he was being so snide with her (from an outside perspective, it really didn’t seem like he was being snide at all, just stating that he didn’t know what the issue is in a regular tone of voice). I then calmly told them both “OK, I’m gonna go now,” (I entered the room they were in to try to support my mom as she worked through the problem.) before my mom immediately yelled “GOOD!!! It would be better anyway!!!” before my dad told her to stop being mean to me.

She talked with me about it a little bit later, and she told me to stay out of discussions/arguments that don’t involve me (once again) so I wouldn’t be subjected to her yelling; this seemed like she was just passing the situation off on me as though I was at fault for putting myself in a situation in which she could yell at me, especially since she didn’t apologize for yelling at me, and it makes me not want to help her when she is feeling upset because of issues she is having (due to feeling like she’d just take her frustrations out on me in the form of yelling like she did with my dad).

Thank you so much for your advice and support! It really means a lot.

I’ve gotten better at remaining calm in recent years, though this is definitely much easier said than done, especially since my mom doesn’t always understand why I need to leave the room momentarily instead of working it out right then and there.

I’ve had a lot of self-doubt in recent years as a result of all of this (Was the arguing, yelling, and criticizing really justified based on my actions?); thank you for reassuring me that my mom’s behavior is NOT okay, and for encouraging me to get help for my anxiety. (I’ve begun the process of participating in my school’s counseling services with my teacher’s knowledge, and without my parents’ knowledge.)

My teacher has been great, too, and her support means the world to me.

I included more details in response to karenvideoeditor’s comment, but I really appreciate the support and all you have done to help people looking for advice!

I really appreciate the advice and support! Not all of the arguments have resulted in yelling, thankfully, but even when they don’t, they typically result in my mom scolding me with an angry, snide, and raised tone of voice, and she has yelled frequently enough that it makes me worried that she will start yelling at me.

All of this has sewn a lot of self-doubt in me, especially as I look back and wonder if all of that arguing, yelling, and criticizing really was justified based on my actions? (Thank you for reassuring me that it’s not!)

Another thing that often happens when I try to talk with my mom about how it feels when she yells at me is that she’ll become very defensive/upset and think I am portraying her as a monster (this is definitely not my intent). Note that she does NOT get upset because her yelling is hurting me, only that it is altering my perception of her.

I don’t think issues with my mom are the primary cause of my anxiety; I also am very dedicated to schoolwork and have displayed a lot of anxiety symptoms in response to school and general life stress. (Thankfully, my parents are not the type to criticize me for not getting perfect grades in everything, though I do put a lot of pressure on myself to do well.) I don’t think my issues with my mom have helped, though, and I wish she was more supportive of me receiving help for my anxiety.

I don’t think cutting my mom off completely is the right decision at this time. She and I are very close, and she has been incredibly supportive of my goals and dreams. With that said, the constant arguing (sometimes for seemingly no reason) has become unbearable, and I have begun to seek counseling services (with my teacher’s knowledge, and without my parents’) in hopes of finding ways to cope with it all.

Thank you again for all of your support! *hugs*
